In what year was Proxima Centauri discovered?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
In what year was Bromine discovered?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.

Gabapentin: Pfizer. Gabapentin is a
central nervous system (CNS) depressant and derivative of the inhibitory neurotransmitter, GABA.
Which country is Focke-Wulf Fw 190 from?
Focke-Wulf Fw 190: Germany. Along with its well-known counterpart, the Messerschmitt Bf 109, the Fw 190 became the backbone of the Jagdwaffe (Fighter Force) of the Luftwaffe.
Who is credited with discovering Barium?
Barium: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
Who is credited with discovering Lawrencium?
Lawrencium: Albert Ghiorso. Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr (formerly Lw) and atomic number 103.
Who is credited with discovering Francium?
Francium: Marguerite Perey. Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.

Sometimes called a nerve impulse or 'spike,' this rapid rise and fall of voltage across a cell membrane ripples to neighboring spots and fires in neurons, muscle cells, and even some plant cells. What is it?
Action potential (also known as a nerve impulse or "spike" when in a neuron) is a series of quick changes in voltage across a cell membrane.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
Largely self-taught, this Dutch tradesman-turned-scientist pioneered the use of the microscope and is commonly called the 'Father of Microbiology' — who is he?
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (AHN-tə-nee vahn LAY-vən-hook, -huuk; 24 October 1632 - 26 August 1723) was a Dutch microbiologist and microscopist in the Golden Age of Dutch art, science and technology.
Despite the name, this gold-brown-eyed black-and-white bird of Australia isn't related to its Eurasian namesake at all — it's a butcherbird cousin in its own genus. What is it?
Australian magpie (Gymnorhina tibicen) is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand, and the Fijian island of Taveuni.
What yellow-green digestive fluid is produced continuously by the liver but stored and concentrated in the gallbladder until it's needed to break down fats in the small intestine?
Bile (from Latin bilis), also known as gall, is a yellow-green fluid produced by the liver of most vertebrates that aids the digestion of lipids in the small intestine.

Making up only about 2.6 percent of the brain's total weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and regulates critical functions like heart rate and breathing. What is it called?
Brainstem (or brain stem) is the posterior stalk-like part of the brain that connects the cerebrum with the spinal cord.

Standing in contrast to the 'cat-like' carnivorans that diversified across Africa and southern Asia, this suborder unites dogs, bears, raccoons, and pinnipeds under one 'dog-like' umbrella — what's it called?
Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.

Appointed royal executioner under Louis XVI and later chief executioner of the First Republic, this Frenchman personally carried out the executions of the king, his queen, and Robespierre — who is he?
Charles-Henri Sanson (French; 15 February 1739 - 4 July 1806), was the royal executioner of France during the reign of King Louis XVI, and later chief executioner of the First French Republic.

Largely self-taught and grinding his own lenses from spare parts on a Kansas farm, this astronomer's homemade skills landed him at Lowell Observatory — where his 1930 survey turned up the first known body in the Kuiper belt; who was he?

Clyde Tombaugh (February 4, 1906 - January 17, 1997) was an American astronomer and telescope maker, best known for discovering Pluto in 1930, marking the first detection of what would eventually be recognized as the Kuiper belt.
Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.

This is the only living group of horses, asses, and zebras — odd-toed, herbivorous mammals whose ancestors first evolved in North America before spreading into Asia, Africa, and South America — what is it?
Equus (genus) is a genus of mammals in the perissodactyl family Equidae, which includes horses, asses, and zebras.
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
In organisms whose total cell count is fixed at maturity, this cell-enlargement process drives nearly all further growth after the embryonic stage — what is it?
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
Home to aromatic herbs like mint, oregano, and lavender as well as the seed crop chia, this family of mostly herbaceous flowering plants is commonly known as the mints or deadnettles — which family?

Lamiaceae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as mints, deadnettles, or sages. The mint family as a whole has a cosmopolitan distribution comprising about 236 genera and around 6,900 to 7,200 species.
Named after a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of rod-shaped bacteria can multiply even at refrigerator temperatures and causes a rare but serious foodborne illness — what is it?
Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Formed from two glucose units linked by an alpha(1→4) bond, which disaccharide, a reducing sugar unlike sucrose, is released when starch breaks down during malting?
Maltose (or), also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an (14) bond.
More than 80% of cases trace to asbestos exposure, and it grows from the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — which cancer is it?
Mesothelioma is a type of cancer that develops from the thin layer of tissue that covers many of the internal organs (known as the mesothelium).
This unique group of mammals is the only one whose members lay eggs rather than bear live young, comprising the platypus and four echidna species — what group is it?
Monotreme are mammals of the order Monotremata.

Encompassing several types of kidney inflammation affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or nearby interstitial tissue, this general medical term falls under the broader category of nephropathy — what's the condition?
Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys and may involve the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue surrounding the glomeruli and tubules.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Ranging from linear chains to heavily branched polymers, these carbohydrate compounds — like starch, glycogen, and chitin — consist of many simple sugar units linked together. What are they called?
Polysaccharide (from Ancient Greek (pols) 'many, much' and (skkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".
Ancient Chinese philosopher Confucius believed this oratorical skill could profoundly move even those not present in the room — what is the term for addressing a live audience?
Public speaking is the delivery of a speech to a live audience.

Covering more than 100 conditions like lupus and Sjögren's syndrome and overlapping heavily with immunology, this branch of medicine tackles inflammation in the joints, muscles and bones — what is it called?

Rheumatology (from Ancient Greek (rhema) 'flowing current') is a branch of medicine devoted to the diagnosis and management of disorders of which the common feature is inflammation in the bones, muscles, joints, and internal organs.
This American painter turned inventor co-developed a telegraph system and became the namesake of the dot-dash code that helped make telegraphy commercially viable — who is he?
Samuel Morse (April 27, 1791 - April 2, 1872) was an American inventor and painter.
The smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds, this small, alert hunting dog's name literally translates to 'brushwood dog,' reflecting its original job of flushing game — which breed?
Shiba Inu (Japanese) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.
Usually diagnosed in infancy, this rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene is the leading inherited cause of death in babies if left untreated — what condition is it?
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder that results in the loss of motor neurons and progressive muscle wasting.
Also called 'true comfrey,' this Boraginaceae perennial is native to damp European meadows and popular with bumblebees, despite carrying warnings about liver toxicity if eaten — which plant?
Symphytum officinale is a perennial flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
This American economist and social theorist, a prominent voice in the conservative movement, received the National Humanities Medal from President George W. Bush in 2002 — who is he?
Thomas Sowell (SOHL; born June 30, 1930) is an American economist, economic historian, and social theorist.

Entering Soviet service in the 1960s, this jet was the USSR's first supersonic bomber to reach production, though it disappointed with poor range and proved notoriously hard to fly — what aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22 (Air Standardization Coordinating Committee name: Blinder) was the first supersonic bomber to enter production in the Soviet Union.

Belonging to the same family as kangaroos, this informally named group of smaller macropods is native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations as far away as Hawaii and the UK — what are they called?
Wallaby is a small or middle-sized macropod native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations in New Zealand, Hawaii, the United Kingdom and other countries.

Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this Chinese strategist was sought out three times by a warlord before becoming chancellor of the Shu Han state and, later, regent to its young second emperor — who is he?

Zhuge Liang (181 AD - September or October 234 AD), courtesy name Kongming, was a Chinese statesman and strategist who lived through the collapse of the Eastern Han dynasty and became the principal architect of the Shu Han state.
This nucleoside, a building block of RNA, gives rise to the energy carriers ATP and ADP and is used as an intravenous drug for certain irregular heartbeats — what is it?
Working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer designed one of history's most famous puzzle games — yet saw no royalties from it until founding a company around it in 1996. Who is he?
Caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, this intestinal infection can spread to the liver and trigger abscesses there even without any prior diarrhea — what condition is it?
Amoebiasis: Human disease caused by amoeba protists.
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.

Among the first life forms on Earth and typically just a few micrometres long, these single-celled prokaryotes thrive everywhere from hot springs to radioactive waste and drive the putrefaction stage of decay — what are they?
This steroid medication treats everything from rheumatoid arthritis to psoriasis, and can even be given to speed a premature baby's lung development before birth — what is it?
Betamethasone: Steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.

Convicted in 2013 for leaking nearly 750,000 classified documents to WikiLeaks while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, this whistleblower had her sentence commuted by President Obama in 2017 — who is she?
Chelsea Manning: American activist and whistleblower (born 1987)
A political scientist studying voter turnout and race, this scholar rose through Harvard's deanships to become its 30th president in 2023 — only to resign months later; who is she?
Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)
Declared one of the world's most invasive species in 2000 and named Australia's top pest problem in 2008, which highly adaptable Asian bird thrives in cities?
Common myna: Bird of the family Sturnidae.
Also known as hawthorn, quickthorn, or May-tree, this genus of several hundred shrub and tree species in the rose family is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Crataegus: Genus of flowering plants in the rose family Rosaceae.

Developed as a successor to an earlier delta-wing fighter family, this French all-weather interceptor entered service with the French Air Force in 1974, equipped with Cyrano IV radar — what aircraft is it?
Dassault Mirage F1: French attack aircraft. During the 1960s, Dassault commenced development of what would become the Mirage F1 as a private venture, alongside the larger Mirage F2.
Native to North Africa and West Asia, this annual herb in the celery family lends its leaves and seeds as both an herb and a spice — what is it?
Dill: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

This medical term covers abnormal cell or organ growth — from hip conditions to bone marrow disorders — and is generally distinguished from cancerous neoplasia, though some forms are precancerous. What is it called?
Dysplasia: Abnormal development, at macroscopic or microscopical level.
Australia's tallest native bird, this flightless species can sprint up to 48 kilometers per hour and often goes weeks without drinking water — which bird?
Emu: Large flightless bird endemic to Australia.
Every animal, plant, fungus and seaweed belongs to this domain, defined by one shared cellular feature: a nucleus wrapped in its own membrane. What are they called?
Eukaryote: Domain of life whose cells have nuclei.
Its 41 living species boast the most varied fur patterns of any land carnivore, all armed with retractile claws and an obligate taste for meat — which family is this?
Felidae: Family of mammals. Felidae ( FEE-lə-dee) is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.

Passed down through generations rather than taught in a classroom, this field covers oral traditions like legends and proverbs as well as customs like festivals and traditional building styles — what is it called?
Folklore: Expressive culture shared by particular groups.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?

Nicknamed for its mole-like digging forelegs and dense fur, this insect widespread across Europe and introduced to the eastern United States is a textbook example of convergent evolution — which species?
Gryllotalpa gryllotalpa: Species of cricket-like animal.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
This extinct archaic human was the first to evolve a humanlike body and gait, the first to leave Africa for Asia and Europe, and the first to wield fire — who were they?
Homo erectus: Extinct species of archaic human. Homo erectus ( lit. 'upright man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
Born in Germany, this businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, beginning operations in San Francisco in 1853 — who is he?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.
With shovel-like front limbs built for burrowing and a mating song broadcast from a specially shaped underground tunnel, which insect is this?
Mole cricket: Members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.
Sold under the brand name Anavar, this synthetic anabolic steroid helps burn victims and Turner syndrome patients gain weight — what is it?
Oxandrolone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It was sold under the brand names Oxandrin and Anavar, among others.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.
This inherited metabolic disorder, caused by mutations in the PAH gene, leaves patients unable to break down a certain amino acid and can give off a musty odor if untreated — what is it?
Phenylketonuria: Amino acid metabolic disorder. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
Caused by viral infections, autoimmune disorders, or pulmonary embolism, this condition inflames the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity, causing sharp pain when breathing — which condition?
Pleurisy: Disease of the lungs. Pleurisy, also known as pleuritis, is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
First prescribed in 1934, this steroid sex hormone plays a key role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development — what is it?
Progesterone: Sex hormone. Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
This is the name for three positive whole numbers a, b, and c satisfying a² + b² = c², like the classic set (3, 4, 5) — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple: Integer side lengths of a right triangle.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.
Known commonly as baking soda, this white crystalline compound with the formula NaHCO3 occurs naturally as the mineral nahcolite — what is its chemical name?
Sodium bicarbonate: Chemical compound. It is a salt composed of a sodium cation (Na+) and a bicarbonate anion (HCO−3).
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Also called the broadbill, this large migratory predator sports a long, flat, pointed bill and can reach nearly 15 feet in length — what fish is it?
Swordfish: Fish which has a long, pointed bill. Swordfish are elongated, round-bodied, and lose all teeth and scales by adulthood.

Believing he'd been commanded to build the biblical Third Temple, this engineer single-handedly created an operating system written in a language he invented himself, despite later struggles with schizophrenia and homelessness — who was he?
Terry A. Davis: American computer programmer (1969–2018)
With the symbol Sn and atomic number 50, this metal emits a crackling 'cry' when bent and boasts more stable isotopes than any other element — which one?
Tin: Chemical element with atomic number 50 (Sn). A metallic-gray metal, tin is soft enough to be cut with little force, and a bar of tin can be bent by hand with little effort.

Once grimly nicknamed the "white death" and historically called consumption, this contagious bacterial disease usually starts in the lungs — and most who carry it never show a single symptom. What is it?
Tuberculosis: Infectious disease. Tuberculosis initially infects the lungs, but it can also spread to other parts of the body.
The primary flavor compound in the vanilla bean, this phenolic aldehyde is now more often made synthetically than extracted from the real pod — what is it?
Vanillin: Chemical compound. Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Native to the Baltic, Black, and Caspian Sea basins, this large freshwater fish's range now stretches from the UK to western China — which species?
Wels catfish: Species of fish. It has been introduced to several countries in Western Europe, Mediterranean and Asia as a prized sport fish.
Ukraine's first female prime minister, she co-led the Orange Revolution and later led the Batkivshchyna party while championing EU integration — who is she?
Yulia Tymoshenko: Prime Minister of Ukraine (2005, 2007–2010)
What is the chemical symbol for lead?
The symbol for lead is Pb. Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb and atomic number 82.
